title: no-throw manifest
description: Colors a package's exported surface. `nothrow.json` sits beside a package's `package.json`; the same shape minus `files` and `package`, nested under a `packages` key, is `nothrow.overrides.json`. Readers ignore unknown fields, and absence of a fact always means the strict reading.

version.description: Bumped only on a breaking reinterpretation. A version this reader does not know floors the whole manifest.

package.description: The npm package these colors are about. Overlays name their target here; it is how an overlay is matched, never by its own npm name.

exports.description: npm export subpath to the symbols reachable through it.

files.description: SRI hashes of the files these colors were written for. Any mismatch floors the manifest; required by `nothrow emit`, absent in overlays.

entry.description: One symbol, covering all of its overloads. Keys are public export names post-aliasing, in a strict JSDoc-namepath subset.

async.description: Whether the declaration was `async`, which declaration emit erases. Default `false`, because absence must mean "might sync-throw".

conditions.description: The access paths over this symbol's own parameters it is non-throwing given. Absence means maximally conditioned; unconditional cleanliness is recorded positively as [].

note.description: Free text the engine ignores; JSON has no comments.

conditionPath.description: Root `param<N>`, then `.member`, `[]` for element access, `.@@name` for a well-known symbol. The grammar is closed.

accessor.description: `false` is a positive record that a declared property really is data. Absence is not that record.
